jobs.description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW
KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds. KKR’s insurance subsidiaries offer retirement, life and reinsurance products under the management of Global Atlantic Financial Group. References to KKR’s investments may include the activities of its sponsored funds and insurance subsidiaries.
TEAM OVERVIEW
The Credit Financing team is part of KKR's Global Macro and Asset Allocation (GMAA) platform and is responsible for developing, structuring, executing, and managing financing solutions across KKR's global credit platform.
The team partners closely with portfolio managers to develop and execute financing strategies that optimize capital structures across private credit funds, BDCs, evergreen institutional vehicles, SMAs, and other investment strategies globally. The team executes financing solutions across the capital structure, including asset-backed lending facilities, middle market CLOs and CLO warehouse facilities, NAV financing solutions, financing solutions for KKR's ABF portfolios, repo facilities, unsecured debt, private placements, and other bespoke financing structures. Beyond transaction execution, the team oversees firmwide liability management.
ROLE OVERVIEW
The Associate/Principal will play a central role in structuring, negotiating, and executing financing transactions across KKR's global credit platform. The role provides exposure to a broad range of financing products and capital structure solutions while partnering with portfolio managers to develop innovative financing strategies.
The Associate/Principal will work closely with portfolio managers, senior management, financing counterparties, legal counsel, rating agencies, and other key internal and external stakeholders to originate and execute transactions, optimize capital structures, and develop innovative financing solutions.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Lead the structuring, negotiation, execution, and ongoing management of financing transactions across KKR's global credit platform.
Drive legal negotiations alongside internal and external counsel for new financings, amendments, extensions, waivers, refinancings, and other strategic liability management initiatives.
Develop and execute financing strategies by evaluating lender appetite, market conditions, and capital structure alternatives.
Build and maintain financial models to evaluate financing economics, borrowing capacity, structural terms, covenant compliance, and transaction risk.
Research new financing products, market developments, and capital structure innovations to broaden KKR's financing capabilities.
Build and maintain relationships with financing counterparties, institutional investors, and syndicate partners.

Troubleshoot Layer 2/Layer 3 incidents end to end — from link flaps and optics through routing and traffic engineering — and drive root cause and lasting fixes
Automate repetitive network tasks with Python, Ansible, or similar tooling where it reduces toil

Experience with modern datacenter vendors (e.g. Arista, Cisco, Juniper, Nvidia/Mellanox)

Network automation (Python, Ansible, Terraform, or similar) used in production
Experience with EVPN, leaf-spine, and large-scale Ethernet fabrics
Prior work supporting rapid datacenter or cluster capacity build-outs
Additional Requirements
Willing to work onsite in Dublin

At Roblox, we’re building the tools and platform that empower our community to bring any experience that they can imagine to life. Our vision is to reimagine the way people come together, from anywhere in the world, and on any device.
We’re on a mission to connect a billion people with optimism and civility, and looking for amazing talent to help us get there.
A career at Roblox means you’ll be working to shape the future of human interaction, solving unique technical challenges at scale, and helping to create safer, more civil shared experiences for everyone.
We are seeking an experienced Senior Software Engineer with a deep background in 3D computer graphics and engine development to join the ML Data Pod within the Foundation AI team. In this role, you will build the foundational infrastructure that powers our next-generation AI capabilities.
As the AI landscape rapidly shifts toward spatial and 3D generation, high-quality data has become the ultimate bottleneck. You will be instrumental in solving this challenge by unlocking the Roblox engine as a massive, scalable platform for synthetic data generation.
This is a unique opportunity to bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI research and low-level engine architecture. You will be navigating unmapped territory—shaping how we represent and structure complex 3D data (such as meshes, materials, lighting, and scene graphs) to effectively train state-of-the-art 3DGen models. Ultimately, the synthetic pipelines you architect will directly fuel the frontier AI models that will define the future of immersive 3D content creation for millions of creators worldwide.
Responsibilities
Synthetic Data Generation:
Spearhead initiatives to leverage the Roblox engine to procedurally generate the massive, high-fidelity 3D datasets required for training frontier 3DGen models.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Partner closely with AI research scientists to translate complex model training requirements into actionable engine features, while collaborating with core engine teams to implement them safely and efficiently.
Pipeline Architecture:
Design, build, and optimize scalable graphics and engine-level systems capable of generating diverse spatial, geometric, and visual data at scale.
Technical Integration:
Drive the technical direction for embedding synthetic data generation workflows into the existing engine architecture without compromising core performance.
Minimum Qualifications
5+ years of experience building and shipping complex, production-grade software systems
Deep expertise in 3D computer graphics, rendering pipelines, and game engine architecture.
Strong proficiency in systems programming (e.g., C++) with a proven track record of writing highly optimized, scalable code.
Experience extracting, modifying, or manipulating programmatic data from within a complex engine environment.
Strong communication skills with a demonstrated ability to bridge the gap between machine learning researchers and low-level systems engineers.
Bonus:
Familiarity with machine learning data pipelines, automated synthetic data generation, or 3D generative AI architectures.
Preferred Qualifications
Background in geometry, linear algebra, or related mathematical domains
Experience with graphics APIs or frameworks a plus but not required

jobs.description: Job Description The Role: At General Motors, the Vehicle Motion Controls and Estimation (VMCC) Platform Design team develops reusable vehicle-motion control and estimation solutions for future vehicle platforms. This role provides technical leadership in either the steering-controls domain or the suspension and vertical-motion-controls domain, depending on the position. The steering focus includes electric power steering (EPS), steer-by-wire, and active rear steering. The suspension focus includes semi-active and active suspension and vertical vehicle motion. In either focus area, you will own the technical domain while helping develop a scalable VMCC platform that supports multiple vehicle configurations, actuator technologies, operating modes, and driver modes. This role is designed for an experienced automotive controls engineer from a leading OEM or Tier 1 supplier who can lead work from vehicle-dynamics analysis through control- architecture and algorithm design and into production software, calibration, and vehicle validation. What You’ll do: Lead end-to-end controls design for either the steering or suspension/vertical-motion domain. Develop reusable control and estimation algorithms that translate vehicle-level motion objectives into actuator commands while accounting for system constraints, operating modes, and degraded operation. For steering-focused positions, develop controls for EPS, steer-by-wire, and active rear steering, including steering response, driver feedback, desired-state and trajectory tracking, disturbance rejection, mode transitions, and fault-tolerant or degraded operation. Translate vehicle-dynamics, ride, handling, stability, comfort, and controllability objectives into control requirements, performance metrics, algorithms, and calibration strategies. Use model-based development, vehicle-dynamics simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), driver-in-the-loop (DiL), and in-vehicle testing to design, calibrate, verify, and validate controls. Implement algorithms in production-oriented embedded software and support requirements development, interface definition, design reviews, diagnostics, and software-release activities. Provide technical leadership, mentor engineers, resolve cross-functional issues, and communicate design decisions across controls, software, systems, calibration, test, and program teams Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) MSc or PhD in Controls, Robotics, Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical Engineering or equivalent degree with relevant experience. 5+ year of relevant experience Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. jobs.description: Amazon's Talent Solutions organization is working to build the earth's best employer — and Work Authorization (WA) is at the center of that mission. The WA team is a group of seasoned subject matter experts who, in close partnership with Legal, Risk & Compliance, Immigration, Technology, and Product teams, protects Amazon from the financial, reputational, and legal risks of unauthorized working across every country in which we operate. Our work is not incidental — it is a front-line defense against regulatory exposure and a foundational pillar of compliant, scalable global hiring. As Manager III, HR Specialist for Work Authorization Operations, you will serve as a single-threaded owner for the operational delivery of work authorization compliance services worldwide. You will lead team managers and process leads who together oversee HR Specialists providing global production support. This is a strategic L6 leadership role — you are expected to set vision and direction, define success, own the multi-year roadmap for your delivery organization, and represent WA Operations with authority in meetings with Legal, Risk & Compliance, Immigration, Technology, and Product stakeholders. You will build and sustain an organization that understands work authorization compliance at a deep, substantive level and that holds itself to an uncompromising standard of accuracy, process integrity, and SOP adherence. You will work in close daily partnership with Regional HR Managers who own the program design and regional compliance strategy. Your accountability is for operational execution, team capability, and the delivery systems that make compliant, high-quality outcomes possible at scale. Together, you and the Regional HR Managers form the leadership backbone of Work Authorization. Key job responsibilities People Management & Leadership Development - Lead, coach, and develop Manager-level direct reports as emerging and established leaders — not just operational supervisors. Invest in their growth as independent problem-solvers, communicators, and people leaders. - Define clear performance expectations for each Manager aligned to both business outcomes and leadership competencies; conduct regular structured feedback conversations and annual calibrations. - Build a succession pipeline within the management team; proactively identify high-potential talent across the organization for development. - Foster a culture of psychological safety, accountability, and continuous improvement. Model the standard you expect: deep curiosity, intellectual honesty, and zero tolerance for compliance shortcuts. - Own the org health of the broader team — including engagement, attrition, capacity planning, and workload equity — and develop mechanisms to proactively surface and address issues before they affect performance. - Partner with your Managers to navigate complex performance management situations, building their capability to have hard conversations and reach fair, documented outcomes. - Drive consistent onboarding and role-readiness standards across all team levels, ensuring new team members are equipped with substantive compliance knowledge — not just process scripts — before handling live casework. Compliance Expertise & Knowledge Management - Develop genuine, deep fluency in work authorization law, regulatory frameworks, and compliance obligations across all operating jurisdictions — not surface-level familiarity. Understand the "why" behind every control, not just the "what." - Champion a compliance-first culture throughout your organization. Make it unambiguously clear that SOP deviations, unauthorized workarounds, and process shortcuts carry serious legal and regulatory risk — and hold that standard consistently. - Partner with Legal and Risk & Compliance to remain current on regulatory changes, and translate those changes into updated operational guidance, retraining, and revised SOPs in a timely and thorough manner. - Build structured knowledge management systems — including tiered training curricula, knowledge assessments, compliance playbooks, and escalation guides — that give the team durable, accessible tools for handling complex, ambiguous situations correctly. - Establish a compliance quality framework: define defect categories, track defect rates by manager and process stream, root-cause recurring issues, and drive targeted remediation programs. - Proactively identify compliance blind spots — areas where the team's knowledge or processes are insufficient to handle emerging business scenarios, regulatory changes, or technology shifts — and address them ahead of risk materialization. - Act as an escalation resource for complex, novel compliance questions that require judgment beyond standard SOPs; partner with Legal when matters exceed operational authority. Operational Excellence & Process Improvement - Own end-to-end accountability for WA operational delivery metrics — including SLA attainment, case quality, throughput, error rates, and customer experience — across all regions and vendor-supported workflows. - Design and maintain a rigorous operating rhythm: daily/weekly/monthly reviews with each Manager layer, structured escalation paths, and clear accountability for metric ownership at each tier. - Lead continuous improvement initiatives using lean and kaizen methodologies; identify and eliminate process waste, redundancy, and error-prone manual steps. - Own the identification and prioritization of process improvement opportunities across all operational streams, including intake, document review, verification, escalation handling, and vendor coordination. - Manage vendor team coordination and performance; ensure vendor SLAs, quality standards, and compliance obligations are met and that escalation paths between vendor teams and internal teams are clear and effective. - Drive standardization across regions to the extent compliance frameworks allow, while accommodating legitimate jurisdictional variation. Eliminate unnecessary divergence that creates training burden or quality risk. - Maintain accurate, real-time visibility into capacity, volume trends, and staffing adequacy; proactively flag and address resource gaps before they affect service levels. Stakeholder Management & Communication - Serve as a confident, knowledgeable representative of WA Operations in cross-functional meetings with Legal, Risk & Compliance, Immigration, Technology, Product, Workforce Staffing, and senior PXT leadership — speaking with authority on operational processes, SLA capabilities, team capacity, and compliance posture. - Maintain a close, trust-based partnership with Regional HR Managers who own program design and regional compliance strategy. Provide them with clear, honest, and timely operational intelligence so they can make well-informed programmatic decisions. - Actively participate in technology and product roadmap discussions; provide substantive input on operational and compliance requirements, edge cases, and scalability needs — not just react to what is built. - Build executive-quality communications —business reviews, escalation narratives — that deliver clear findings, data-backed conclusions, and actionable recommendations to senior stakeholders. - Earn trust with cross-functional partners through demonstrated expertise, consistent follow-through, and straightforward communication about what is and is not operationally feasible. - Represent WA Operations in OP planning, headcount discussions, and budget processes; clearly articulate the operational implications of business growth, regulatory changes, or technology gaps. - Own and manage escalation intake from internal business partners including recruiters, HRBPs, Workforce Staffing, and senior business leaders; ensure escalations are triaged, routed, and resolved promptly with proper root cause capture. Strategic Planning & Execution - Define, instrument, and regularly review success metrics for the WA Operations organization — including compliance defect rates, SLA attainment, team capability benchmarks, and experience outcomes for candidates and employees. - Contribute substantive input to OP1/OP2 planning cycles: author or co-author sections covering operational health, investment needs, risk landscape, and capacity requirements with precision and strategic clarity. - Partner with Technology and Product teams to shape the WA technology roadmap; ensure that planned technology investments solve real operational and compliance problems and that the team is prepared to adopt and leverage new capabilities effectively. - Identify and proactively address structural risks to program continuity: knowledge concentration, single points of failure, vendor dependency, and compliance gaps in emerging business areas. - Build the case for organizational investment — headcount, tooling, training, process redesign — with rigorous data, clear business rationale, and connection to compliance risk reduction and operational performance improvement. - Maintain awareness of regulatory and business trends globally; partner with Legal, Regional HR Managers, and Global WA Service Leader to ensure the operational organization stays ahead of — not reactive to — changes in the compliance landscape.

jobs.description: Job Description: Pacific Life is investing in bright, agile, and diverse new talent to contribute to our mission of innovating our business and creating a superior customer experience. We're actively seeking a talented Institutional Marketing Strategy Director to join our Institutional Retirement Solutions Group (IRSG). This role can be based in Newport Beach, CA, Omaha, NE, or another approved Pacific Life office location. As Institutional Marketing Strategy Director, you will serve as a strategic marketing partner to IRSG leadership, helping translate business strategy, market dynamics, customer needs, and competitive intelligence into clear marketing priorities and differentiated market strategies. The role spans Pacific Life's institutional retirement businesses, including Pension Risk Transfer (PRT), Defined Contribution Lifetime Income (DCLI), Stable Value, and emerging retirement solutions. You will help leadership determine where Pacific Life should focus, how the organization should position itself, which audiences and opportunities matter most, and how marketing can influence growth. You will bring together market intelligence, customer and audience insights, competitive understanding, positioning, messaging, thought leadership, and go-to-market strategy to help IRSG build preference and strengthen its position in the marketplace. This is a highly visible leadership role at the intersection of business strategy, market intelligence, marketing strategy, and growth . The ideal candidate is equally comfortable analyzing a market, challenging a business assumption, shaping a narrative, and translating strategy into action. How You'll Help Move Us Forward: Lead and Evolve Institutional Marketing Strategy Own, activate and evolve the established IRSG marketing strategy, ensuring it remains aligned with business priorities, market opportunities, customer needs, and the maturity of each business. Partner with senior business and functional leaders to identify the markets, audiences, opportunities, and priorities where marketing can have the greatest impact. Translate business strategies and established marketing priorities into actionable audience strategies, positioning, messaging, content, and go-to-market recommendations. Evolve strategic direction along with business goals and strategies for the Institutional content roadmap, ensuring priority themes, audiences, and timing are informed by business objectives, market and customer insights, and go-to-market needs, while partnering with the broader marketing team on development and execution. Develop business-specific marketing approaches that recognize the distinct needs and market positions of Pension Risk Transfer (PRT), Defined Contribution Lifetime Income (DCLI), Stable Value, and emerging institutional businesses while maintaining alignment with the established IRSG narrative and strategy. Monitor market, business, and competitive developments and recommend strategic adjustments as priorities and opportunities evolve. Lead ongoing marketing planning and prioritization, establishing clear trade-offs and aligning marketing resources, investments, and activity to the highest-value business priorities and measurable growth objectives. Drive Market Intelligence and Competitive Insights Serve as a strategic consumer of market, customer, and competitive intelligence, bringing relevant insights into IRSG marketing and business discussions. Partner with internal strategy, analytics, research, product, distribution, and other teams to identify and leverage available market and customer insights. Monitor key industry, competitor, regulatory, and market developments and assess their implications for IRSG marketing priorities and business objectives. Identify gaps in market or customer understanding and help define the research or analysis needed to inform strategic decisions. Translate complex market and competitive information into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for business and marketing leaders. Bring an external perspective to marketing strategy, helping identify emerging opportunities, shifts in audience needs, and potential areas of differentiation. Steward Positioning, Messaging, and Market Narrative Serve as a steward of IRSG's established positioning, value proposition, and overarching narrative, ensuring they are consistently and effectively applied across marketing initiatives. Translate established positioning and value propositions into audience-specific messaging and marketing strategies for PRT, DCLI, Stable Value, and emerging institutional businesses. Partner with business and product leaders to apply the established positioning to priority initiatives, launches, campaigns, and market opportunities. Identify opportunities where changing market dynamics, customer needs, or competitive activity may warrant refinement or evolution of existing positioning and messaging. Ensure consistency and differentiation across institutional marketing efforts while allowing messaging to reflect the distinct needs and maturity of each business. Partner with other marketing teams to bring the established positioning and narrative to life across channels and experiences. Guide Institutional Thought Leadership Provide strategic direction for institutional thought leadership priorities, ensuring they align with the established IRSG marketing strategy, narrative, positioning, and business objectives. Partner with business leaders and subject matter experts to identify priority topics and opportunities where thought leadership can support market engagement and business goals. Translate business priorities and market developments into recommendations for thought leadership themes, audiences, channels, and timing. Partner with operations, digital and other marketing resources to ensure thought leadership initiatives are strategically focused and effectively executed. Advise on executive visibility, industry engagement, conferences, speaking opportunities, and other external opportunities based on business and marketing priorities. Evaluate the effectiveness and relevance of thought leadership efforts and recommend adjustments as business priorities and market dynamics evolve. Inform Go-to-Market and Growth Initiatives Provide strategic marketing leadership for new products, market expansion efforts, strategic initiatives, and emerging growth opportunities. Assess market readiness, audience needs, competitive dynamics, and differentiation opportunities to inform go-to-market strategies. Partner with product, distribution, communications, analytics, digital, and other marketing teams to translate strategy into execution. Help define target audiences, market priorities, value propositions, and channel strategies for priority initiatives. Provide strategic marketing counsel on business cases, executive presentations, strategic communications, and other high-priority business materials. Identify opportunities to strengthen the connection between marketing activity and the customer and distribution journeys that influence growth. Measure Impact and Evolve the Strategy Establish frameworks for evaluating marketing effectiveness, market impact, and progress against strategic priorities. Define meaningful KPIs for marketing strategies, thought leadership initiatives, market engagement, and priority growth programs. Use data, analytics, research, and business results to evaluate what is working and where strategy should evolve. Regularly assess the effectiveness of marketing investments and recommend changes in priorities, resources, or approach. Champion a culture of accountability, learning, and continuous improvement across institutional marketing. The Experience You Bring 10+ years of experience in strategic marketing, financial services marketing, institutional marketing, business strategy, consulting, product marketing, market intelligence, or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience developing marketing strategies that are directly connected to business growth and strategic priorities. Strong understanding of institutional financial services, retirement markets, insurance, investments, asset management, or related B2B financial markets. Experience translating market, customer, competitive, and business intelligence into strategic recommendations. Proven ability to influence senior leaders and build alignment across complex, matrixed organizations. Experience developing positioning, segmentation, value propositions, messaging, go-to-market strategies, or related strategic marketing frameworks. Exceptional communication, presentation, and storytelling skills, with the ability to make complex subjects clear and compelling. Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to move from insight to recommendation to action. Demonstrated ability to operate strategically while working effectively with teams responsible for execution. The experience you bring: Experience in Pension Risk Transfer, Defined Contribution, retirement income, Stable Value, asset management, insurance, or adjacent institutional markets. Experience working with institutional buyers and influencers, including consultants, intermediaries, advisors, plan sponsors, institutional investors, recordkeepers, or retirement-focused organizations. Experience building or leading market intelligence, competitive intelligence, customer insight, or strategic planning capabilities. Experience developing thought leadership strategies and executive positioning programs. Experience supporting large-scale growth, transformation, innovation, or new-market initiatives. MBA or advanced degree preferred. What Makes You Stand Out You think beyond the marketing function. You understand how markets, customers, competitors, products, distribution, and business strategy come together to create growth. You are naturally curious. You want to understand what is changing in the market, why it matters, and what Pacific Life should do about it. You turn complexity into clarity. You can take a complicated business issue or market dynamic and turn it into a clear point of view, strategic recommendation, or compelling story. You connect strategy to action. You know when to stay at the strategic level and when to translate strategy into specific priorities for the teams responsible for execution. You can influence without owning everything. You build trust with senior leaders and cross-functional partners and can move work forward in a highly matrixed environment. You understand that differentiation is earned. You look beyond claims and messaging to identify the capabilities, perspectives, and market opportunities that can create meaningful competitive advantage. You bring executive presence. You are comfortable challenging assumptions, presenting recommendations, and engaging with senior leaders on complex business and market issues. Why This Role Matters This role serves as the strategic marketing connector across IRSG—bringing together business priorities, market intelligence, customer insight, competitive understanding, and marketing execution to ensure the organization's marketing strategy remains aligned to business needs and responsive to the marketplace. With the IRSG marketing strategy and overarching narrative established, the Director will help activate and evolve that strategy across Pension Risk Transfer, Defined Contribution Lifetime Income, Stable Value, and emerging retirement solutions. The role will translate strategic priorities into focused marketing initiatives, inform future planning through ongoing market and competitive intelligence, and ensure that marketing efforts are differentiated, audience-relevant, and connected to measurable business outcomes. The position will also look beyond the current roadmap, identifying emerging market opportunities, shifts in customer and competitive dynamics, and future strategic needs that should inform the next evolution of IRSG's marketing strategy. Ultimately, this role ensures that marketing operates as a strategic business partner—not simply an execution function —helping IRSG strengthen market position, build preference, and support sustainable growth.
